title: Replacing Polybutylene Piping with CPVC in a Raleigh Home

locations.name: Raleigh, North Carolina (crawl space context)
locations.basis: Transcript explicitly states Raleigh, NC and notes crawl spaces in the area.

summary: This Old House’s Ask This Old House episode documents a PB (polybutylene) piping replacement in a Raleigh, NC home. The segment outlines the historical prevalence of polybutylene in the 1970s, the leaks observed in PB and acetal fittings, and the decision to replace the entire PB network with CPVC hot- and cold-water lines. The crew removes the old piping through wall openings, reroutes new CPVC from the crawl space, and ties into fixtures (notably a second-floor shower valve) using brass-to-CPVC adapters and threaded/female adapters. The project requires extensive wall and ceiling access, drywall repair by a skilled tradesperson, and a final water test. The host commentary frames the replacement as both technically necessary and time-consuming, emphasizing that labor and wall restoration are major cost components alongside materials. The episode also places the work in a regional context, noting that tens of thousands of Raleigh-area homes were affected by PB piping.
